synthesis.description: A dated credit report on counterparty exposure is produced and Darron Giron forwards it, usually the same day, under a subject such as "Credit Report--2/22/01", with occasional pendings lists. Recipients mostly read it. Sometimes reports go out late or in a catch-up batch after an absence. Later rounds raise questions about content: a list missing the transport positions, and whether figures are quantities at price or calculations.
steps: The credit report for the business day is generated with its date in the title.
The distributor checks the report arrived and is the right date.
The report is forwarded to the standing recipient list.
Recipients review exposure and raise questions on missing positions or how figures are derived.
Missed days are resent together when the distributor returns or systems recover.
synthesis.approach: Schedule the credit report to publish and email itself to the distribution list once the daily run completes, with a check that the report date matches the business day and an alert when the run fails, so nothing waits on one person forwarding it. Add a short legend stating which position types are included and how figures are calculated.
synthesis.rationale: The manual part is a daily check-and-forward that one person carries; a short checklist (confirm date, confirm all position types including transport, send, log late days) keeps it consistent when someone covers and reduces the content questions that follow.
